title: GSplit: Scaling Graph Neural Network Training on Large Graphs via Probabilistic Splitting
problem: Mini-batch GNN training with data parallelism causes significant redundant feature loading and computation because the same graph vertices appear in multiple GPU micro-batches, limiting scalability to large graphs.
motivation: On large graphs like Orkut and Papers100M, data-parallel GNN training loads up to 2.5x more features than necessary due to vertex overlap across micro-batches; eliminating this redundancy can dramatically reduce training time.
method: Split parallelism: each mini-batch is sampled once and non-overlappingly partitioned (split) on-the-fly among GPUs using an offline probabilistic splitting algorithm. The offline phase uses pre-sampling to weight graph vertices and edges by expected sampling frequency, then applies weighted min-edge-cut partitioning (METIS) to find a global vertex-to-GPU assignment. Online splitting maps each sampled vertex to its pre-assigned GPU in constant time. Inter-GPU feature shuffles at each GNN layer exchange only required features.
key_novelty: Online probabilistic splitting that reduces NP-hard per-mini-batch partitioning to a constant-time lookup by leveraging an offline pre-sampled weighted graph partition, providing provable expected communication minimization and load balancing.
contributions: Split parallelism paradigm eliminating redundant vertex loading and computation in GNN mini-batch training
Lightweight online splitting algorithm with probabilistic guarantees via offline pre-sampling and METIS partitioning
GSplit split/shuffle API compatible with existing single-GPU GNN sampling and training kernels
Up to 4.4x speedup over DGL, 4.1x over P3, 1.9x over Quiver on large-graph benchmarks

metrics.speedup: Up to 4.4x over DGL (2.5x average), 4.1x over P3 (2.4x average), 1.9x over Quiver (1.4x average) on Orkut/Papers100M/Friendster graphs
metrics.accuracy: No accuracy loss vs data-parallel training (verified on Papers100M)
metrics.other: Hardware: AWS EC2 p3.8xlarge with 4x NVIDIA V100 GPUs

limitations: Offline pre-sampling and METIS partitioning add one-time preprocessing cost; gains depend on graph redundancy (less benefit on low-overlap graphs like Friendster); multi-host setup reverts to hybrid DP+split.
